doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Orchestra dates and unusual instruments
summary: He notes orchestra dates in LA, miking strings and brass, and never adding a lute.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: think I ever added a lute to anything but at some times I’d make a note for an English horn or a bassoon or something like that. That would be the orchestra dates. And then whatever the instrument I wanted to feature, sometimes a couple of French horns or something like that, we’d have to mic certain ways. There’s a real technique to micing a string section in an orchestra, brass and woodwinds, that type of thing. But I would make notes about — I’d put bassoon question mark you know, and then we’d come back. And I did the orchestra dates in LA. That’s where I added that sort of thing. I don’t think I ever added a lute to anything. I know I’ve worked with Irish groups and we had the pennywhistles and the whistles and the uilleann pipes and all that kind of stuff. If I had a lute on a song I’m not familiar with it.
